primarySuggestion.name: PP Impact Copolymer (PP-B, talc/EPDM modified)
primarySuggestion.reasoning: Part geometry (large, thin-shell 2.5–3.5mm, organic Class-A double-curvature surface, envelope size ~1.7m x 0.65m) is characteristic of an automotive exterior bumper fascia. PP-B (impact copolymer, often talc/EPDM modified) is the overwhelming industry-standard resin for bumper fascias due to low cost, flexibility, paintability and impact performance at high volume (200,000 units/yr). No metadata/filename signal for a premium resin (PC/ABS) was found, so standard PP-B is assumed.

processRecommendations.reasoning: User-forced ground truth. Thin uniform-ish shell wall, large projected area, and high production volume (200k/yr) are all consistent with single-cavity high-tonnage IM production typical of automotive bumper fascias.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Undercuts detected relative to Z draw direction will lock the part in a single-action tool.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Add hydraulic side-action sliders/lifters or re-orient parting line to eliminate undercuts where possible.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Wall thickness variation drives differential shrinkage, causing warpage on this very large thin panel.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Normalise wall to constant nominal (e.g. 2.8mm ±0.2) and add ribbing instead of thickening for stiffness.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Faces with no draft along pull direction will scuff/gall on ejection and increase cycle time via slow ejection.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Apply minimum 1–2° draft on all vertical faces not defining Class-A surface.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Single-gate fill of a 1.69m part in thin wall (2.5mm) risks short shots, high injection pressure and visible weld/flow lines.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Use multi-gate hot runner (sequential valve gating) to balance fill and hide weld lines in low-visibility zones.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: High polish/finish requirement increases mould manufacturing cost and cycle-to-cycle finish sensitivity.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Specify SPI A-1/A-2 finish steel and plan for post-mould painting to mask minor surface defects.

dfmIssues.description: 4 undercut faces detected relative to the Z draw axis, plus 2 zero-draft faces — the part cannot release from a simple 2-plate tool as modelled.
dfmIssues.impact: Requires side-action sliders/lifters, increasing mould cost by 15-30% and adding maintenance wear points; risk of part damage on ejection if unaddressed.
dfmIssues.fix: Re-orient parting line along the natural bumper wrap, or add hydraulic slide cores for the undercut regions; apply minimum 1.5° draft globally.

dfmIssues.description: Measured wall varies from 2.53mm to 3.54mm across the shell (σ=5.3), well above the ±10% uniformity guideline for a part this large.
dfmIssues.impact: Differential cooling/shrinkage causes warpage and visible sink on the A-surface, driving scrap and secondary straightening/painting rework.
dfmIssues.fix: Redesign to a constant nominal wall (~2.8mm) with ribbing for local stiffness rather than local thickening.

dfmIssues.description: Part length of ~1.69m fed from limited gate positions creates a very long flow-length-to-thickness ratio for a 2.5mm nominal wall.
dfmIssues.impact: High injection pressure requirement, risk of short shots, visible weld lines and increased clamp tonnage (~5000T class press estimated).
dfmIssues.fix: Use a hot-runner multi-gate (valve-gated, sequential) system to balance flow and relocate weld lines to non-cosmetic zones.

dfmIssues.description: 492 of 498 faces are free-form B-spline Class-A surfaces requiring high-grade polish and tight tolerance CNC/EDM machining of the cavity/core.
dfmIssues.impact: Increases mould build cost/time (~15-20%) and requires additional trial/polish iterations before PPAP sign-off.
dfmIssues.fix: Lock surface data early (Class-A validated), specify SPI A-1 finish and plan additional tool-trial cycles into programme timeline.

dfmIssues.description: Typical bumper mounting bosses and clip features (not explicitly modelled in this B-rep) commonly cause sink marks when fed from thin nominal wall.
dfmIssues.impact: Cosmetic sink visible after paint, potential rejection on visible surfaces.
dfmIssues.fix: Rib/boss wall ≤60% of nominal wall thickness, use core-out and gate proximity control to manage local shrinkage.

analysis.aiExplanation: This part is a large (1.69m x 0.65m x 0.53m), thin-shell (2.5-3.5mm), highly free-form (492/498 B-spline faces) plastic component consistent with an automotive bumper fascia. Per user-forced ground truth, injection moulding is the process. Material is inferred as PP Impact Copolymer (PP-B), the industry-standard resin for bumper fascias, absent any explicit resin callout. Geometry-derived deterministic values (wall thickness, projected area, tooling cost estimates, manufacturability score) were used verbatim as instructed. Cavity count of 1 reflects the part's large single-piece envelope; family/multi-cavity tooling is impractical at this size despite the 200,000 unit/yr volume, so annual output is met via short cycle time (~15s) on a single very-large-tonnage press. Undercuts, non-uniform wall and long flow length are flagged as the dominant manufacturability risks.
analysisLimitations: Resin grade was not specified in the source data; PP-B was inferred from geometry/part type, not confirmed from a drawing or filename tag.
Cavity count of 1 assumes single large-part tooling; actual production may use family tooling or geometry differs from a simplified B-rep, which could change projected area and tonnage estimates.
Wall thickness statistics (2.53–3.54mm) were derived from an automated shell analysis and may not capture localized boss, rib, or clip features not explicitly modelled.
Mould cost, mould life, and runner weight are parametric estimates based on part size/complexity class and have not been validated against a detailed tool design.
Machine tonnage and press class were estimated from projected area and typical cavity pressure for PP-B; actual tonnage requirement should be confirmed via mould-flow simulation.

dfmIssues.description: Draft -1° below 1° minimum — Zero/negative draft means the part cannot release — it drags, scuffs and jams on ejection.
dfmIssues.fix: Add ≥ 1° draft to all vertical faces (more for deep or textured walls); increase toward 5° for heavy grain.

dfmIssues.description: 4 undercuts need side-actions / lifters — Each undercut adds a slide or lifter — raising tool cost, maintenance and cycle time, and capping cavitation.
dfmIssues.fix: Design out undercuts with pass-through cores / bump-offs where the resin allows, or consolidate them onto one moving side.

dfmIssues.description: Flow-length/wall 668 exceeds ~200 (L/t) — Beyond the resin's L/t limit the melt freezes before filling — short shots, high pressure and weak weld lines.
dfmIssues.fix: Add gates to shorten each flow path, thicken flow leaders, or select a higher-flow (higher-MFI) grade.

deterministicAnalysis.aiExplanation:
Derived deterministically for injection_moulding from the measured geometry. No AI call was made; every figure below is arithmetic on a measurement or a library lookup, and each states its own basis.

  • injectionMoulding.wallThicknessMm = 2.5 — thin-shell wall from 2·V/S (ray-cast overshot the cavity) (non-uniform uniformity) [geometry, imm-wall]
  • injectionMoulding.projectedAreaCm2 = 10946.8 — projection: bbox face × √fill for a solid, bbox face (worst case) for a shell [geometry, imm-area]
  • injectionMoulding.ejectTimeSec = 2 — mould open + eject + close, standard toggle press [rule, imm-eject]

Still open (1):
  • Which resin is this moulded in? — The geometry is the same whichever resin fills it, but the resin sets the weight, the £/kg and the cooling time — and cooling is most of the cycle. The 2060 cm³ measured here weighs 1.854 kg in PP Impact Copolymer (PP-B) and 2.904 kg in POM / Acetal (Delrin).
analysisLimitations: Unanswered: Which resin is this moulded in?

DFM checks ran against the measured geometry. Checks that need a drawing callout — tolerances, which face is critical, whether a weld line is in a load path — did not run, so this list is a floor and not a ceiling.
